market_pulse.note: Around $60,190 at 10:16 AM ET Saturday, up almost 9% from an overnight low of $55,252, its lowest since September 2024 (The Crypto Basic); Eurasia Business News had it near $60,280, up about 1.4%, while at 6:55 AM ET it was $58,091, down 6.0% over 24 hours (Ted Pillows).
Around $1,691, up about 2.2% in a Saturday snapshot (Eurasia Business News); earlier it traded at $1,650, down 5.6% over 24 hours, after a low near $1,550 (Ted Pillows; CryptoPotato).

Fell below $2 trillion on Saturday for the first time in more than two years, per CoinMarketCap data, about $900 billion lower than a few weeks ago; CoinCodex put it near $2.00 trillion, down 5.4% over 24 hours, at 1 AM ET (CryptoPotato; CoinCodex).
About 58.1% on CoinMarketCap's measure Saturday morning; Ted Pillows put it at 57.5%, down from 58.1%, and CoinCodex had 56.2% (CryptoPotato; Ted Pillows; CoinCodex).

themes.title: Bounce back to $60,000
themes.summary: Bitcoin climbed back above $60,000 Saturday morning after dropping to about $55,300 overnight; it remains about 52% below its October 2025 record of $126,080 (Bitcoin.com News; Eurasia Business News).

themes.title: Billions in liquidations
themes.summary: About $2.4 billion to $2.67 billion of leveraged positions were wiped out over 24 hours, mostly longs, including more than $1 billion in Bitcoin futures, per CoinGlass data (Bitcoin.com News; Eurasia Business News).

themes.title: ETF outflows
themes.summary: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs had about $1.25 billion of net outflows over the five sessions from Nov. 16 to Nov. 20, including $124.5 million on Friday (Ted Pillows; Bitcoin.com News).

themes.title: Tech selloff and Fed worries
themes.summary: The Nasdaq fell 5.3% Friday and about 10% for the week, and hot October inflation data raised fears of a December Fed rate increase (Bitcoin.com News; CoinGabbar).

themes.title: Extreme fear
themes.summary: The Crypto Fear and Greed Index read 12, unchanged from Friday and in extreme fear, compared with 68 a month ago (Ted Pillows; CoinGabbar).

categories.name: Majors (BTC/ETH)
categories.note: Both rebounded Saturday, with Bitcoin up about 1.4% and Ether about 2.2% in a midday snapshot, after roughly 10% drops overnight (Eurasia Business News; CoinCodex).

categories.name: Large-cap altcoins
categories.note: Solana led the rebound, up about 3.7% to $70.86, and XRP rose about 2.2% to $0.93; Hyperliquid (HYPE) slipped 0.4% to $61.28 (Eurasia Business News).

categories.name: Crypto stocks
categories.note: Strategy closed Friday at $77.80, down 9.7%, and Coinbase fell 6.3% to $101.97; for the week Strategy lost about 30% and Coinbase and Robinhood about 20% each (Ted Pillows; Bitcoin.com News).

categories.name: Stablecoins and DeFi
categories.note: Stablecoin market cap held near $280 billion, down 0.4%, while DeFi market cap fell 5.6% to about $53 billion, per CoinGecko data (CoinGabbar).

watch_list.why: Bitcoin is trying to hold $60,000 after lows near $55,250; a Sunday weekly close below about $65,350 would mark a seventh straight weekly decline (The Crypto Basic; Ted Pillows).
MSCI is set to remove Strategy (MSTR), a large Bitcoin holder, from some U.S. indexes after the close on Nov. 30 (CoinStats).
Spot ETFs do not trade on weekends; October PCE inflation data is due Nov. 25, ahead of the Dec. 9 Fed decision (Admirals; Bitcoin.com News).

movers.name: Solana (SOL)
movers.note: Up about 3.7% to near $70.86 in a Saturday snapshot, the strongest of the large tokens tracked (Eurasia Business News).

movers.name: XRP (XRP)
movers.note: Up about 2.2% to near $0.93 (Eurasia Business News).

movers.name: Ethereum (ETH)
movers.note: Up about 2.2% to near $1,691 (Eurasia Business News).

movers.name: Bitcoin (BTC)
movers.note: Up about 1.4% to near $60,284 after an overnight low near $55,250 (Eurasia Business News; The Crypto Basic).

movers.name: Hyperliquid (HYPE)
movers.note: Down about 0.4% to near $61.28, the only decline among the large tokens shown (Eurasia Business News).

movers.name: Zcash (ZEC)
movers.note: Down about 19.1% over 24 hours as of 1 AM ET, the biggest loser in the top 200 (CoinCodex).
